text:
Priya K: kicking off tabletop drill — simulating a P0 latency spike affecting embeddings-store. this is a practice run, no real pages will be sent. please follow the runbook and treat updates as if live. :rotating_light:
IncidentBot: [SIMULATION] page fired for channel #incidents — incident_id=sim-20260212-01, symptom=embeddings-store high tail latency, severity=P0. triggered at 2026-02-12T17:09:00Z.
Sam H: ack — i'm oncall and will handle initial triage. reading runbook now.
Priya K: Sam, focus on customer impact assessment and an initial status page blurb. Jorge, you're on communication lead for this drill.
Sam H: quick checks: recent deploys ✅, rptd errors on metrics show 99th pct latency jump from 200ms -> 2.3s, memory pressure normal. hitting embedding backend shard 7.
Jorge L: copying a status page draft for dry-run — please critique: 
```
Status: Degraded performance for embeddings API
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency and request timeouts for embedding calls; embeddings under heavy load may queue.
Detected: 2026-02-12T17:09:00Z
Scope: subset of requests routed to embeddings-store shard 7 (rolling deploy affected)
Mitigation in progress: rolling back last deploy to revert regression; enabling fallback model (embed-lite-v2) for affected routes; autoscaling additional pods.
Next update: 30 minutes or earlier as new info becomes available.
```
Sam H: nit: change "request timeouts" -> "sporadic timeouts" and add "no data loss reported" line. also include link to docs/runbook: https://intranet.redwood/ops/embeddings-runbook
Jorge L: updated: added "no data loss". also wrote a concise customer-facing message for the incident page: 
> We're investigating higher than normal latency for the Embeddings API. Some requests may be delayed or time out. Our engineering team is actively investigating and mitigation steps are underway. We'll post updates here every 30 minutes.
Priya K: good. during drills we want the customer message to be short, non-technical and set cadence. avoid rollback details in customer note (keep in internal updates).
Sam H: handing off primary oncall to Jorge for comms so I can continue root cause. Handoff summary: observed latency spike at 17:09, suspicion on recent quantization change in shard 7; metrics pinned to deploy-2026-02-12T16:50. no error-rate increase, just tail latency. I've initiated rollback but paused to let comms draft stabilise.
Jorge L: taking over comms. I'll post the simulated status page and trigger the templated customer notification via the dry-run workflow.
Oncall Rotation Bot: reminder — oncall escalation policy applied: P0 -> page primary -> if >10m no ack -> escalate to secondary. This is a drill; follow dry-run checkbox.
Priya K: exercise objective checklist: 1) post public status page draft, 2) send customer-safe notification dry-run, 3) practice internal playbook update message, 4) collect feedback. Mark which items we completed.
Sam H: completed 1 & 3 in my head; posting internal update now: 
- Severity: P0 (drill)
- Owner: Sam H (handoff to Jorge L for comms)
- Impact: Increased tail latency on embeddings; sporadic timeouts for a subset of customers; no data loss.
- Actions taken: paused recent deploy on shard 7; prepared rollback; scaled replicas + enabled embed-lite-v2 fallback; monitoring duration.
- Next steps: finalize rollback if latency doesn't improve in 10m; prepare postmortem template if rollback doesn't resolve.
Jorge L: sending simulated customer email (dry-run) for review: 
> Subject: We're investigating intermittent delays with Embeddings API
>
> Hi —
> We're aware that some requests to the Embeddings API may be experiencing intermittent delays. Our engineers are actively investigating and working on mitigation. We do not believe any customer data has been affected. We'll send an update within 30 minutes.
>
> — Redwood Inference Status Team

Priya K: feedback on customer email: tone good, shorten "we're aware" -> "we're investigating" and remove "may be" to be more confident: "We are investigating intermittent delays." Add link to status page. Also add contact path for enterprise customers: support@redwood.com
Sam H: lesson note — keep escalations aligned: if rollback happens, communications must say "mitigation applied" not specific remediation details.
Jorge L: posting mock public status page (dry-run) now, tagging #product and #support for visibility :point_down:
[POSTED MOCK STATUS PAGE LINK - DRY RUN]
Priya K: exercise complete for live updates. please fill quick feedback: what went well, what was confusing, suggested template edits.
Sam H: went well: handoff concise, oncall metrics check was quick. confusing: where to link runbook in customer-facing comms vs internal. suggestion: internal update should include a single canonical runbook link and a one-line summary for the public status.
Jorge L: suggested template edits: - reduce internal template verbosity, add explicit fields for "customer-facing blurb" and "enterprise contacts", - add checkbox in comms composer for "avoid technical remediation details"
Priya K: follow-ups assigned (drill retrospective): 1) update status page template w/ 'customer blurb' field (owner: Jorge) 2) add runbook link shorthand to comms playbook (owner: Sam) 3) automate fallback-model toggle into runbook (owner: infra team).
Oncall Rotation Bot: drill metadata recorded: drill_id=drill-2026-02-12-embeddings, duration=~12m, participants=5.
Priya K: thanks all — great run. drop any lingering feedback here. :white_check_mark:
